sub_theme: Settling into Year 1 / All About Me

lessons.title: Introducing Ourselves in Year 1
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to listen to others and respond appropriately in a whole-class discussion.
success_criteria: I can sit and listen without interrupting.
I can answer a question about myself.
I can ask a friend a question.
lessons.starter_activity: Circle time: pass a soft toy and each child says their name.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model good listening behaviour and turn-taking; discuss why Year 1 might feel different from Reception.
lessons.independent_task: In pairs, children take turns sharing one fact about themselves and their summer, then feed back to the class.
key_questions: What is different about Year 1?
What did you enjoy about the summer?

differentiation.support: Adult provides a sentence starter to complete
differentiation.greater_depth: Ask a follow-up question to their partner unprompted

lessons.assessment_notes: Note listening stamina and confidence speaking in front of the class — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Recap one new thing learned about a classmate.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family one thing you're looking forward to in Year 1.

lessons.title: Counting and Ordering Numbers to 10 (Recap)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count, read, and order numbers to 10 confidently.
success_criteria: I can count objects to 10.
I can order numbers 1-10.
I can read numerals to 10.
lessons.starter_activity: Count around the circle to 10 and back down.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting a set of objects, touching each once, then writing the numeral. Recap number order using a number line.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a worksheet ordering scattered numerals 1-10 and counting sets of objects to match.
key_questions: What number comes after 6?
How do you know this set has 8 objects?

differentiation.support: Order numbers 1-5 with a number line for reference
differentiation.greater_depth: Order numbers to 20 and find missing numbers in a sequence

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline check of counting/ordering to inform planning — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire 'what number am I?' clue game.
lessons.home_link: Practise counting to 10 and beyond together.

lessons.title: My Amazing Body
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name at least five parts of the human body.
success_criteria: I can point to and name five body parts.
I can label a simple body diagram.
lessons.starter_activity: Sing 'Heads, Shoulders, Knees and Toes'.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Recap body part names from EYFS, introducing a few new ones (elbow, wrist, ankle, shoulder).
lessons.independent_task: Children label a body outline diagram with as many body parts as they can, using word banks for support.
key_questions: What body part helps you run?
Can you find your elbow?

differentiation.support: Word bank with matching pictures provided
differentiation.greater_depth: Label 10+ body parts independently including internal ones like heart

lessons.assessment_notes: Note vocabulary range and labelling accuracy — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Quick body-part pointing game.
lessons.home_link: Name body parts together while getting ready for bed.

lessons.title: Self-Portrait Drawing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to draw a self-portrait showing key facial features in proportion.
success_criteria: I can draw a face with eyes, nose, mouth and hair.
I can use the right colours for my features.
lessons.starter_activity: Look closely in a mirror at facial features.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model drawing a simple face, discussing proportion (eyes halfway down the face, etc.).
lessons.independent_task: Children draw a detailed self-portrait using mirrors for reference, adding colour.
key_questions: Where do your eyes sit on your face?
What colour is your hair?

differentiation.support: Use a pre-drawn face outline to add features to
differentiation.greater_depth: Add background/context detail and shading

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe attention to proportion and detail — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.plenary: Display portraits and admire as a class gallery.
lessons.home_link: Draw a family member's portrait together.

lessons.title: Story Time: A New Class Story
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer retrieval questions about a story read aloud.
success_criteria: I can answer a question about what happened in the story.
I can say who the characters are.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict the story from the front cover.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a story about starting a new school year aloud, modelling stopping to ask retrieval questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer simple retrieval questions about the story verbally or by drawing, in small groups.
key_questions: Who is the main character?
What happened at the start of the story?

differentiation.support: Answer with pointing to pictures
differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences with evidence from the text

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2, informing initial reading assessment.
lessons.plenary: Recap the story's key events in order.
lessons.home_link: Read a book together and ask one question about it.

lessons.title: One More, One Less to 10
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find one more or one less than a number to 10.
success_criteria: I can find one more than a number to 10.
I can find one less than a number to 10.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap counting to 10 with actions.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model finding one more/less using a number line and physical counters.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete one more/one less problems using counters and a number line, recording answers.
key_questions: What is one more than 5?
What is one less than 9?

differentiation.support: Use physical counters throughout with 1:1 support
differentiation.greater_depth: Extend to numbers to 20 and explain reasoning without counters

lessons.assessment_notes: Record one more/less fluency — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire one more/less oral quiz.
lessons.home_link: Practise one more/one less with toys or snacks.

lessons.title: What Do We Need to Stay Healthy?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name things humans need to stay alive and healthy.
success_criteria: I can name three things humans need to survive.
I can name one thing that keeps us healthy.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what happens if we don't eat or drink.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss basic needs for survival (food, water, air, shelter) and things that promote health (exercise, sleep, hygiene).
lessons.independent_task: Children sort picture cards into 'needed to survive' and 'helps us stay healthy', recording their sorting.
key_questions: What do humans need to survive?
What keeps us healthy?

differentiation.support: Sort with 2-3 obvious examples
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the difference between surviving and being healthy

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of basic needs vs health promotion — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Recap the difference between needs and healthy habits.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a healthy habit your family has.

lessons.title: Colour Mixing Introduction
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to mix primary colours to create secondary colours.
success_criteria: I can name the primary colours.
I can mix two primary colours to make a new colour.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap primary colours (red, yellow, blue).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Demonstrate mixing pairs of primary colours to create orange, green, and purple.
lessons.independent_task: Children experiment mixing paint colours, recording which combinations make which secondary colours.
key_questions: What happens when you mix red and yellow?
Can you predict what blue and yellow will make?

differentiation.support: Adult supports mixing with clear 1:1 ratios
differentiation.greater_depth: Experiment with varying ratios to create different shades

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe understanding of colour mixing — evidence for ART.1/SCI (materials links).
lessons.plenary: Recap which colours make which secondary colours.
lessons.home_link: Mix colours with paint or coloured pencils at home.

lessons.title: Writing About My Summer
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a simple sentence about their summer using capital letters and full stops.
success_criteria: I can say my sentence aloud before writing it.
I can start with a capital letter.
I can end with a full stop.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap capital letters and full stops with example sentences.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model composing and writing a sentence about the summer, saying it aloud first.
lessons.independent_task: Children write one to two sentences about their summer holiday, checking for capital letters and full stops.
key_questions: What did you do this summer?
Does your sentence make sense when you read it back?

differentiation.support: Adult scribes while child dictates, child copies underneath
differentiation.greater_depth: Write 3+ sentences using conjunctions like 'and'

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline writing assessment — check letter formation, capital letters, full stops — evidence for ENG.W1/W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share sentences with a partner and check each other's punctuation.
lessons.home_link: Write one more sentence about something fun from the summer.

lessons.title: Naming 2D Shapes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name and describe properties of common 2D shapes.
success_criteria: I can name a circle, square, triangle and rectangle.
I can count the sides of a shape.
lessons.starter_activity: Shape hunt around the classroom.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/recap 2D shape names and count sides/corners together.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort shape pictures by name and record the number of sides for each.
key_questions: How many sides does a triangle have?
What shape has four equal sides?

differentiation.support: Focus on circle, square, triangle only
differentiation.greater_depth: Include pentagon, hexagon and compare properties

lessons.assessment_notes: Record shape name and property recognition — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire shape naming game using real objects.
lessons.home_link: Find and name 2D shapes around your home.

lessons.title: What Season Is It Now?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify the current season and describe its features.
success_criteria: I can name the current season.
I can describe two features of this season.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what the weather has been like recently.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the four seasons and discuss features of the current season (likely early autumn).
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and label features of the current season, recording weather observations.
key_questions: What season is it now?
How do you know?

differentiation.support: Simple picture-based recording
differentiation.greater_depth: Compare current season to a different season in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline seasonal awareness assessment — evidence for SCI.SEA, to build on across the year.
lessons.plenary: Start a class weather/season observation journal.
lessons.home_link: Observe and describe today's weather with your family.

lessons.title: Introducing an Artist: Self-Portraits by Famous Artists
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a similarity and difference between two artists' self-portraits.
success_criteria: I can name one thing I notice about an artist's self-portrait.
I can compare two self-portraits.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a famous self-portrait (e.g. Van Gogh) and discuss initial reactions.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Show 2-3 famous self-portraits (e.g. Van Gogh, Frida Kahlo), discussing style differences.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss in pairs and record one similarity and one difference between two self-portraits shown.
key_questions: What do you notice about this self-portrait?
How is it different from this other one?

differentiation.support: Simple verbal comparison with adult support
differentiation.greater_depth: Write a sentence comparing the styles

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observational and comparative skill — evidence for ART.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the artists' names and one fact about each.
lessons.home_link: Look up a famous painting together and discuss what you notice.

lessons.title: Phonics Baseline: Phase 5 Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read Phase 5 tricky words and CVC/CCVC words.
success_criteria: I can blend sounds to read a word.
I can read at least 3 tricky words on sight.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick-fire flashcard recap of Phase 5 graphemes.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Recap alternative graphemes (e.g. 'ai', 'ay', 'a-e') and model blending words containing them.
lessons.independent_task: Children read a set of levelled words/sentences, with the teacher noting fluency for baseline assessment.
key_questions: Can you blend this word?
Do you know this word by sight?

differentiation.support: Focus on simple CVC words with 1:1 support
differentiation.greater_depth: Read longer words with multiple alternative graphemes

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline phonics assessment to group children for the term — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress and recap key graphemes.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading phonics flashcards sent home.

lessons.title: Comparing Length
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare the length of two or more objects using appropriate vocabulary.
success_criteria: I can say which object is longer/shorter.
I can order 3 objects by length.
lessons.starter_activity: Compare the length of two pencils by eye.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing length directly (placing objects side by side) and using non-standard units.
lessons.independent_task: Children measure and compare classroom objects using cubes as non-standard units, recording results.
key_questions: Which object is longer?
How many cubes long is this object?

differentiation.support: Compare 2 objects only
differentiation.greater_depth: Order 4+ objects and use standard units (rulers) to measure

lessons.assessment_notes: Record measurement and comparative language use — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of longest/shortest objects measured.
lessons.home_link: Compare lengths of objects at home using cubes or hand spans.

lessons.title: What Are Objects Made Of?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify the material an everyday object is made from.
success_criteria: I can name the material of an object.
I can sort objects by material.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss the difference between an 'object' and a 'material' using an example (a chair is wood).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce common materials (wood, plastic, metal, glass, fabric, paper) with examples of objects made from each.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort a collection of objects by material, recording their sorting in a table.
resources_needed: Collection of everyday objects made from varied materials
key_questions: What material is this made from?
Can two different objects be made from the same material?

differentiation.support: Sort 3-4 materials with picture support
differentiation.greater_depth: Sort 6+ materials and justify choices

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of object vs material distinction — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap key materials learned.
lessons.home_link: Find 3 objects at home made from different materials.

lessons.title: Exploring Line and Pattern
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create different types of lines and use them to form a pattern.
success_criteria: I can draw straight, wavy, and zig-zag lines.
I can repeat a pattern of lines.
lessons.starter_activity: Practise drawing different line types in the air.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model drawing straight, wavy, zig-zag and dotted lines, then combining them into a repeating pattern.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own line pattern artwork using a variety of line types.
key_questions: What type of line is this?
Can you repeat your pattern?

differentiation.support: Trace given line patterns before creating own
differentiation.greater_depth: Combine 4+ line types into a complex repeating pattern

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe pattern-making and line control — evidence for ART.1/MATHS.GEO (pattern links).
lessons.plenary: Display and compare line pattern artworks.
lessons.home_link: Look for line patterns on fabrics or wallpaper at home.

lessons.title: Show and Tell: My Favourite Thing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to speak clearly in front of the class about a chosen topic for a short time.
success_criteria: I can talk for a short time about my favourite thing.
I can answer one question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models a short show-and-tell about a favourite item.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a good show-and-tell (clear voice, eye contact, interesting details).
lessons.independent_task: Children take turns presenting a favourite item/topic to a small group, answering one question.
key_questions: What is your favourite thing and why?
Can you tell us more about it?

differentiation.support: Adult prompts with questions throughout
differentiation.greater_depth: Present to the whole class confidently, unprompted

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline spoken language assessment — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Vote on an interesting fact learned from show-and-tell.
lessons.home_link: Practise your show-and-tell talk with family.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Number and Shape
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply number and shape skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can count, order and compare numbers to 10.
I can name 2D shapes and their properties.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's key maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of number ordering, one more/less, and shape properties.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations: number ordering, one more/less, shape sorting, completing a short recording sheet at each.
key_questions: What number is one more than this?
What shape is this and how many sides does it have?

differentiation.support: Adult-led rotation with reduced complexity
differentiation.greater_depth: Independent completion with extension challenges at each station

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 1 baseline maths assessment for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/MATHS.GEO.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate a great first week of Year 1 maths.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting and shapes over the weekend.

lessons.title: Science Review: Our Bodies and Needs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall body parts and survival needs learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name 5 body parts.
I can name 3 things humans need to survive.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's science vocabulary with actions.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering body parts and survival needs.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet labelling body parts and listing survival needs.
key_questions: What body part is this?
What do we need to survive?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided
differentiation.greater_depth: Add additional detail/explanation independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline science assessment for the term — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's science learning.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned in science this week with your family.

lessons.title: Art Review: My Year 1 Art Journal Cover
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a decorative cover page reflecting their art learning this week.
success_criteria: I can use colour mixing and line patterns I learned this week.
I can create a design I am proud of.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap colour mixing and line pattern skills from the week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss creating a cover page combining this week's skills (colour mixing, line patterns).
lessons.independent_task: Children design a cover page for their art journal using mixed colours and line patterns.
key_questions: What skills from this week will you include?
What are you most proud of in your design?

differentiation.support: Adult supports layout planning
differentiation.greater_depth: Combine multiple techniques independently with a personal theme

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of the week's art skills — evidence for ART.1, forming the first entry in ongoing art assessment.
lessons.plenary: Class gallery walk of art journal covers.
lessons.home_link: Show your art journal cover to your family and explain your design choices.
